title: WPSS/956/2021 of PINKEE Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
IN HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND
AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition No.956 of 2021 (S/S)
Km. Pinkee and others .....Petitioners
Vs.
State of Uttarakhand & others ...Respondents
Advocate: Mrs. Neetu Singh, Advocate with Mr. Vinod Chandra, Advocate for the petitioner.
 Mr. Pradeep Hariya, Addl. C.S.C. for the State of Uttarakhand.
 Mr. Lalit Samant, Advocate for the Commission.

Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
 To be precise the factual backdrop is being considered in the light
of the pleadings which had been raised in Writ Petition (S/S) No.896 of 2021.
2. The facts, which has been brought on record is that for the purposes
of conducting the selection process as against 1218 post of Forest Guard, the
respondents had resorted to the process of selection, which included the conduct
of written examination also, looking to the number of candidates, who had
responded to the advertisement dated 21.05.2018, there were various centers
which were assigned to the respective candidates, in order to enable them to take
up their written examination for their assessment of eligibility, to be considered
for appointment on passing of the written examination.
3. The petitioners of these writ petitions have submitted, that the
respective centers the details of which has been given in the writ petition, were
not the centers, which were identified, against, which there was any set of
allegations, that these centers and the candidates who had appeared therefrom,
were at all found to be engaged in cheating or copying of answer sheets in the
process of written examination, which was conducted on 16.02.2020. Hence, the
petitioners submit that on that ground, that the centers which were not involved
in any practice of unfair means in the examination, there cannot be a
witholdment of the process of selection for the centers from where they have
taken their examination and which were not the centers, which had been

2
demarcated by the respondents or identified by the respondents for having being
engaged in the copying process.
4. The petitioners further submit, that as a consequence of the mass
allegation levelled against candidates, who have taken the examination for the
Forest Guard, there was a FIR registered being FIR No.75 of 2020. In this FIR,
the name of the candidate who were involved in the cheating in the examination,
which was conducted on 16.02.2020, were disclosed by the respondents, but
however the said FIR, was put to challenge before the Coordinate Bench of this
Court in C482 Petition No.720 of 2021 & C482 No.721 of 2021 and the
Coordinate Bench vide its judgment dated 09.04.2021, had quashed the
Criminal Case No.75 of 2021 and as a consequence thereto, the petitioners who
were alleged to be involved in any unfair cheating were exonerated of their set
of allegations levelled for commission of offences punishable under Section
420, 120-B IPC, Section 66-D of the I.T. Act and Section 9/10 of U.P. Public
Examination (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act 1998. As a consequence of the
effect of the judgment of 09.04.2021, as far as the petitioners of Writ Petition
No.956 of 2021 (S/S) are concerned, they cannot be said to be involved in
commission of any criminal offence because which stood quashed by the
Coordinate Bench vide its judgment of 09.04.2021, hence the individual set of
allegations was also not made out against the petitioners.
5. The counsel for the petitioners had submitted that the mass copying
in the center from where the petitioners have taken the examination i.e.
Rashtriya Inter College, Sitapur Haridwar; Saraswati Vidhya Mandir, Inter
College, Mayapur, Haridwar; Jwalapur Inter College Jwalapur, Haridwar &
Arya Inter College, Haridwar, were not the one of the centers in which the re-examination was ever directed to be conducted by the respondents, as it has been
done in relation to the other centers where an allegation of mass copying was
found. In that eventuality, since the petitioner's center was not identified, as to
be a center, where the mass copying was held, or as a consequence of an
identification of a center, indulged in mass copying they were directed to
conduct re-examination, since there was no order as such, coupled with the fact
that the criminal set of allegations against the petitioners levelled in Criminal
Case No.75 of 2021, had been quashed by the Coordinate Bench of this Court

3
on 09.04.2021 in C482 No.720 of 2021 consequently, as on date there is no
legal embargo or any impediment as such to curtail, the declaration of result of
the petitioners, which the petitioners were provisionally permitted to undertake
as a consequence of the interim order which was passed by this Court on
02.08.2021. The petitioners submit that as a consequence of the interim order of
02.08.2021, they were provisionally permitted to participate in the physical
examination, but in compliance of the direction contained therein, the result of
the petitioners have been kept in a sealed envelope and the same has not yet
been opened. But the petitioners submit that under the changed circumstances,
as of now, since there is no legal embargo as such to keep the result in the sealed
envelope, the respondents are directed to open the result of the petitioners and
declare the same as directed to be sealed by an order dated 02.08.2021 and in an
eventuality if the petitioners satisfy the eligibility conditions and had qualified
the examination, the respondents may proceed accordingly for considering the
grant of appointment, if they have qualified the examination.
6. Subject to the aforesaid observations, the writ petition stands
disposed of accordingly.
 (Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
 02.03.2022
